headline: US launches ninth consecutive night of Iran strikes, driving Brent crude to $90.15 pre-market and sharpening September Fed-hike odds to ~53%.
stance: Geopolitics vs. earnings: two forces pulling in opposite directions. Energy is the dominant macro risk — a ninth straight night of US strikes on Iran, Iranian ballistic-missile retaliation across four Gulf states, and Brent crude crossing $90 pre-market are all stoking inflation fears that push back any near-term Fed pivot. The offset is strong corporate earnings: TSMC reported Q2 EPS of $4.31/ADR (+77% year-over-year) last Thursday, keeping the AI-chip narrative intact even as index-level semis remain choppy. Net result: a tentative, tech-led open with a hawkish rates backdrop that limits upside on duration-sensitive assets.

news.head: 9th Iran Strike Night
news.body: US Central Command confirmed a ninth consecutive evening of strikes on Iran Sunday, after the death of another American service member in Iraq; Iran responded with ballistic missiles and drones targeting sites in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, and Iraq.

news.head: Brent Hits $90
news.body: Brent crude is trading near $90.15 pre-market (+2.33%), its highest since mid-June, as the Strait of Hormuz closure fears and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports intensify supply-disruption concerns.

news.head: Fed Hike Odds Climb
news.body: Markets are now pricing roughly a 53% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September — up from 47% a day earlier — as surging oil prices threaten to re-ignite consumer inflation after June CPI had offered a brief relief signal.

news.head: TSMC Q2 Blowout
news.body: Taiwan Semiconductor reported Q2 2026 revenue of $40.20 billion (+34% year-over-year) and EPS of $4.31/ADR (+77% year-over-year), beating consensus; the company guided Q3 with continued steep ramp of 2-nanometer technology.

news.head: Trump Confirms 17 US Deaths
news.body: President Trump confirmed the US troop death toll has climbed to 17 since the conflict began, signaling the military campaign against Iran will persist.

news.head: Consumer Sentiment Recovers
news.body: The University of Michigan consumer sentiment gauge rose to 54.4 in July — up nearly 10% from June and the best reading since the Iran conflict began in February — though one-year inflation expectations eased only modestly to 4.2%.

implications: Brent above $90 pre-market re-opens the 'oil re-inflates, Fed hikes' loop that hurt equities in mid-July; energy and refiner stocks are the direct beneficiary, while long-duration tech faces a valuation headwind from higher real rates (currently 2.31% as of the prior cash close).
TSMC's blowout Q2 — $40.2B revenue, 67.7% gross margin, +77% EPS — confirms the AI chip order book is intact; the company is a setup name with company insiders have been buying as of the last scan.

The 10-year yield closed at 4.55% on Friday (prior cash close) and the 2-year at 4.18%, keeping the curve in positive territory at +37 basis points — meaning longer-term borrowing costs exceed short-term rates, a sign of modest growth expectations, but the gap remains thin relative to history.
Gold (prior cash close $4,023) is under structural pressure: higher real rates (2.31%) and a firmer dollar erode the appeal of non-yielding metal; the week prior saw gold lose more than 3%.

Positioning: In rates, speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3-month SOFR futures (3rd percentile of a 3-year range) — a contrarian floor for short-end rate bulls. Speculators are heavily positioned long in 2-year Treasuries (85th percentile) — a contrarian warning for that trade. In equities, Russell 2000 futures show speculators have almost no bullish bets left (2nd percentile) — a contrarian floor for small-caps if sentiment shifts. In commodities, WTI crude specs are at a 3-year low in net longs (6th percentile) even as spot oil surges — classic short-squeeze setup; copper specs are extended long (91st percentile) — a contrarian warning. In FX, speculators are near historically extended short positions in both the British pound (6th percentile) and euro (13th percentile) — contrarian floors for sterling and the euro.

watch.head: Strait of Hormuz Headlines
watch.body: Any diplomatic signal — or further escalation — around the Strait of Hormuz will move oil, inflation expectations, and Fed hike odds in real time today; there are no scheduled US economic data releases Monday.

watch.head: Fed Speaker Circuit
watch.body: With no data on the calendar, FOMC commentary is the primary rate-market driver; hawkish remarks could push September hike odds above 53% and pressure long-duration equities.

watch.head: Semis After TSMC Beat
watch.body: Watch whether TSMC's blowout results lift the broader semiconductor complex (SMH was -6% on the week into Friday) or whether geopolitical chip-supply fears and the mid-July sell-off in the sector cap any bounce.

watch.head: WTI $83-$84 Level
watch.body: WTI crude (pre-market ~$83.55) approaching the $84–$85 range could accelerate refiner outperformance and weigh further on consumer-discretionary names sensitive to gasoline prices.

watch.head: JPY at Extreme
watch.body: The Japanese yen (prior cash close 162.35 ¥/$) is at the 99th percentile of its 3-year range — an extreme level of yen weakness; any BOJ intervention signal or safe-haven yen buying on geopolitical shock could cause a sharp reversal.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: 4.55% (prior cash close, Jul 17); 2-year yield: 4.18% (prior cash close) — the curve is +37 basis points positive, meaning investors demand more yield to lend long-term than short-term, a slight growth-confidence signal.

Real interest rates — what you earn after inflation — stand at 2.31% (prior cash close), a historically high level that raises the hurdle rate for stocks and pressures gold and other non-yielding assets.

10-year inflation breakeven at 2.24% (prior cash close) implies the bond market expects inflation to average just above 2% over the next decade — relatively contained, but oil's surge could push this higher intraday.

Fed balance sheet is growing at just 1.26% year-over-year (as of Jul 15) and the overnight reverse-repo facility has drained to essentially $0.1 billion — meaning excess liquidity that was once a market tailwind has been fully absorbed.
September Fed hike probability has risen to ~53% as oil prices re-accelerate — the Fed is now more likely than not to tighten again if Brent holds above $90.

Financial conditions remain accommodative: the Chicago Fed ANFCI reads -0.535 (as of Jul 10, where negative means easier-than-normal conditions) and the St. Louis FSI at -0.88 (as of Jul 10), providing a cushion against tightening fears.
sections.positioning: In rates, speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3-month SOFR futures (3rd percentile, 3-year range) — a contrarian floor. Separately, speculators are heavily positioned long in 2-year Treasuries (85th percentile) — a contrarian warning; if the short end sells off on hike repricing, that trade faces unwind pressure.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 futures: ~7,498 pre-market (prior cash close: 7,457.69 on Jul 17); Nasdaq 100 futures: +0.43% pre-market (prior cash close NDX: 25,520.24); Dow futures: roughly flat (prior cash close DJI: 52,146.42).

Breadth is mixed but not deteriorating: 61% of S&P 500 members trade above their 50-day moving average and 66.5% above their 200-day (both as of Jul 17 prior cash close), suggesting the rally has meaningful internal support even if headline indices pulled back from recent highs.
NDX breadth is narrower: only 42.6% of Nasdaq 100 names trade above their 50-day moving average — the mega-cap AI leaders are carrying the index while the broader tech complex is under pressure.

VIX at 18.77 (prior cash close) — the market's 'fear gauge' — is calm by historical standards, suggesting options markets are not pricing an acute shock despite the geopolitical noise; VXN (Nasdaq volatility) at 29.03 is more elevated, consistent with the semis sell-off.

SKEW at 147.3 (prior cash close) reflects elevated demand for downside protection (put options) relative to upside calls — large institutional players are hedging tail risk even as VIX stays moderate.

Valuations remain stretched: the Shiller CAPE ratio stands at 41.52 (prior cash close), well above long-run averages, and the equity risk premium is negative at -2.05% — meaning stocks are priced to deliver less return than bonds, a structural vulnerability if rates rise further.
TSMC Q2 EPS of $4.31/ADR beat consensus of ~$3.83, with Q3 guided for continued 2nm ramp; this is a positive read-through for AI chip demand across the semiconductor ecosystem.
sections.positioning: Russell 2000 futures: speculators have almost no bullish bets left (2nd percentile of 3-year range, with hedgers and specs at opposite extremes) — a contrarian floor for small-caps; a catalyst such as a de-escalation headline or Fed pivot signal could trigger a sharp squeeze in the most-shorted small-cap names.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — World's dominant AI chip foundry. Q2 EPS of $4.31/ADR beat consensus by ~13%, revenue +36% YoY; insider buying flagged on back-to-back scan dates (Jul 16–17); company insiders have been buying; stock trades above its 200-day moving average. Shorts are light (1.8 days to cover) — low squeeze risk but clean long setup on AI capex confirmation.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield vs. investment-grade spread at 271 basis points (as of Jul 16 prior cash close) — above 270 bps the credit market is signaling mild caution, but not stress; investment-grade spreads at 78 bps are still historically tight, meaning corporate borrowers face little premium over Treasuries.

The commercial paper funding spread (a measure of short-term corporate borrowing stress) sits at just 29 basis points (prior cash close) — near benign levels, consistent with no acute funding squeeze.

Bank reserves at $3,142.7 billion (as of Jul 15) remain ample, the Treasury's cash account (TGA) holds $756.2 billion, and the reverse-repo facility is near zero — net liquidity backdrop is neutral to slightly supportive for risk assets.
Bank credit growth at 5.98% year-over-year (as of Jul 8) and syndicated loan yields near 6.96% (as of Jul 16) reflect a functioning but not aggressive lending environment.
The SOFR-OIS and FRA-OIS spreads both read -1 basis point (prior cash close) — essentially at zero — confirming there is no interbank stress or counterparty fear in the short-term funding market.
M2 money supply growing at 5.58% year-over-year (as of May) provides a moderate liquidity backdrop; Fed balance sheet growth at 1.26% year-over-year is no longer a meaningful incremental tailwind.

single_name.note: Jefferies Financial Group (JEF) — Mid-sized investment bank. Company insiders have been buying. Shorts are light (1.17 days to cover) — minimal squeeze risk. Fits the credit/financial sector theme given tight spreads and recovering capital-markets activity.
